messages:
mike: Heads-up — noticed p95 for /v1/generate jumped ~140ms right after the routing-fallback rollout at 18:02 UTC. Dashboard shows p50 steady, p99 unchanged. Any ideas? link: https://console/redwood/d/abc123
sara: Did we change sampling or the aggregation window with that rollout? p95 is sensitive to midtail shifts.
olga: Not that I know of. The rollout only changed fallback weighting between dedicated and hosted pools (weight 0.8 -> 0.6). Could be more requests moved to hosted.
jia: If requests hit hosted, kv-cache hit rate will drop for long-running sessions which can inflate p95. Can you pull a slice by route origin?
mike: Tried that. The route-origin breakdown in the UI shows a slight bump for hosted but not enough to explain +140ms. Also quota-fallthrough events spiked.
ux_katie: From a UX angle, users are confused by p50/p95 panels not showing fallback attribution. Maybe we need a small badge that toggles "include fallback" vs "by origin".
olga: Agree. Also, the percentile derivation docs say p95 uses merged t-digest from sampled traces — if sampling rate changed during the rollout we could see p95 move even with tiny origin shift.
sara: Good call. Mike, can you run the raw-samples query for that 10m window? Something like:
```
select sample_latency_ms, route_origin, fallback_reason, quota_status from latency_samples
where endpoint='/v1/generate' and ts between 1724680920 and 1724681520 limit 10000;
```
mike: Running now, posting a trimmed output: first 6 rows show fallback_reason != null for ~12% of samples and those have median ~220ms vs 90ms for non-fallback.
jia: That lines up — fallback samples are midtail heavy. Two things to consider: 1) surface a p95_excluding_fallback and p95_by_origin metric; 2) re-evaluate fallback weighting thresholds so we don't push 12% through the slower path.
ux_katie: For console changes, we can add a small inline toggle and a tooltip: "Exclude quota/fallback samples from percentile" and a link to docs. Low visual clutter.
olga: One more caveat: if the hosted model variant has different max_tokens or runs different quantization, tokenization time differences can appear in per-request latency. Were model variants swapped during the rollout?
mike: No variant swap. Only routing weight and a small queue-size tweak on dedicated (max inflight 64 -> 80).
sara: Queue increase could reduce latency on dedicated but makes it eligible for more fanout into hosted when quota hits. Hard to reason without a combined view.
jia: I'll add a one-off debug panel: p50/p95/p99 split by {route_origin, fallback_reason, model_variant} for that window. If we see p95 drop substantially when excluding fallback samples, we can mark this as telemetry-induced and not a real regression.
mike: Thanks. If it’s telemetry-induced, we still need to call out in release notes so SRE and customer-facing channels don't panic. Could we also add an alert rule that fires only when p95_excluding_fallback increases?
ux_katie: Yep — we can expose that metric as a computed series and let teams wire alerts. I'll mock the toggle and tooltip in the console PR today.
deploy-bot: rollout/routing-fallback v2 deployed by olga at 2024-11-23T18:02:14Z :rocket:
mike: Sweet. Jia/Olga/Sara—ping me when the debug panel is up and I'll re-check the slice. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
